sections.h2: What sets Hamilton County apart for a home seller?
sections.html:
Hamilton County is the metro heart of southeast Tennessee. The Tennessee River winds through Chattanooga, the county seat, and the Georgia line forms the southern edge. Only a few counties in the country share a boundary with ten others, and this is one. The General Assembly created it on October 25, 1819, and by the 2020 count it was fourth in the state for population. Lookout Mountain with Point Park and Ruby Falls draws visitors, and Interstates 24 and 75 are the main arteries.

Beyond Chattanooga, the county holds Collegedale, East Ridge, Lakesite, Red Bank, Ridgeside and Soddy-Daisy as cities, plus the towns of Lookout Mountain, Signal Mountain and Walden. Who collects your tax and at what rate depends on which of these your address falls in.

Census QuickFacts puts numbers on the county:

  • 390,833 people in July 2025, 6.5 percent more than in April 2020
  • 176,983 homes and apartments, with 63.9 percent occupied by owners
  • $312,800 as the middle value of an owner's home in the 2020 to 2024 survey period
  • $76,183 as household income, and 37.5 percent of adults holding a bachelor's degree or more
  • 1,887 building permits in 2025

Compare that $312,800 with $207,500 in Greene County and $210,900 in Hamblen County, and you can see why a tax bill here weighs more.

sections.h2: Who bills and who collects property tax in Hamilton County?
sections.html:
One office values, one body sets the rate, and one office collects. The Assessor of Property appraises, the Board of Commissioners picks the county rate, and the Trustee sends bills and takes payment. The Trustee sits in Room 210 of the courthouse on Georgia Avenue in Chattanooga and runs a second counter at 6125 Preservation Drive, Suite 101, in the Bonny Oaks Industrial Park. Both open from eight to four on weekdays. Call (423) 209-7270.

The Trustee also bills for Collegedale, East Ridge, Lakesite, Red Bank, Ridgeside, Soddy Daisy and Walden. Chattanooga does its own billing through the City Treasurer at City Hall, 101 E 11th Street, Room 100. That office answers at (423) 643-7262 or ptax@chattanooga.gov. A house in Chattanooga therefore gets two separate bills.

Marty Haynes is the Assessor of Property, at 6135 Heritage Park Drive, (423) 209-7300. His office's FAQ points out that it only sets values. When a bill goes up and the value did not move, the cause is a higher rate.

sections.h2: What is the Hamilton County property tax rate?
sections.html:
On June 3, 2025 the county mayor and the assessor announced a certified rate of $1.51 per $100 of assessed value, replacing $2.23. They described it as the lowest since 1941 and said it followed the four-year reappraisal. It went on the bills mailed in fall 2025. The assessor estimated that roughly two thirds of owners would pay the same or less county tax than they did in 2024. Their release adds that state law forces a lower certified rate after a reappraisal so that rising values do not create a windfall, although local governments may raise it again.

Chattanooga's tax page lists a separate city rate of 1.93 per $100. Houses count at one quarter of appraised value for tax purposes, and commercial buildings at two fifths. So a Chattanooga home appraised at $312,800 has an assessed value of $78,200. Divide that by 100, then multiply by the county rate and again by the city rate to see the two bills. Phone the Trustee to learn the rate printed on this year's notice.

sections.h2: When are Hamilton County taxes due and what is the penalty for paying late?
sections.html:
Notices go out in late September, and the payment window opens October 1 and stays open through the last day of February. In mid-November 2026 the window is open and no interest has built up. Starting March 1, the county adds 1.5 percent a month, which it describes as 18 percent a year.

The Trustee's FAQ gives practical rules:

  • You may pay in part, and the office accepts partial payments
  • For mailed checks, only a postmark by the deadline counts, and the office's own meter stamps are rejected
  • Online payments are treated as made on the day of the transaction
  • Any First Horizon Bank in the county will take a current-year payment if you bring the original bill

No state rule makes the county mail a notice, and the Trustee says a missing one does not erase interest. Chattanooga uses a different late schedule, charging 1 percent interest and a half percent penalty each month, and it hands unpaid earlier years to the Chancery Court in March. Taxes that stay unpaid can end up at the county's June tax sale, which carries a one year redemption period.

sections.h2: How can I challenge my Hamilton County property value?
sections.html:
Talk to the appraisers first. Look up your parcel on the Assessor's property search and sales comparison tools, or ring 423-209-7990 to discuss it with a staff appraiser. The Assessor wants informal review requests in before May 20.

Still unhappy? Ask the Assessor's office for the form to appear before the county Board of Equalization. That board meets during June and takes filings into the first week of the month, so confirm the closing date by phone. A later stage is the State Board of Equalization, where an administrative judge hears the case. The owner has to prove the number, and the state says matched sales of similar homes make the strongest evidence.

Hamilton County revalues on a four-year cycle. The latest round took effect in 2025, and the next one is set for 2029. In the years between, the Comptroller's schedule still lets an assessor fix mistakes in ownership, location or physical description when the owner asks before March 1.

sections.h2: What relief programs apply to Hamilton County owners?
sections.html:
Tennessee refunds a slice of the tax to low-income seniors, disabled homeowners and disabled veterans. The county's FAQ quotes a $37,530 income ceiling for 2025. The state's 2026 brochure raises that to $38,470 of 2025 income, with a $33,600 value cap for seniors and disabled owners and $175,000 for veterans. Hamilton County says it matches what the state pays. To book a time, call the Bonny Oaks office at (423) 209-7799.

The freeze for owners 65 and older follows different lines. The county government is missing from the Comptroller's list of 28 freeze counties, yet Chattanooga adopted one in 2017 and uses a 2026 income limit of $63,470. It reduces only the city bill. For land used for farming or forestry, the Assessor runs the Greenbelt program, which requires 15 acres or more.

sections.h2: How does the property tax bill work when I sell in Hamilton County?
sections.html:
Bills are addressed to the owner of record. The Trustee advises new owners to read their closing statement or call the title company, since what each person owes turns on the transfer date, and an unpaid balance stays with the parcel. Before you list, ask the Trustee's office for the balance on each tax year, plus any city balance if the house is in Chattanooga.

If you inherited the home or fell behind, the title company can pay what you owe from your proceeds at the closing table. The Register of Deeds, reachable at (423) 209-6560, records the deed and collects the state transfer tax.

faqs.q: What is the Hamilton County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county's certified rate for 2025 was $1.51 per $100 of assessed value, replacing $2.23. Chattanooga's page shows its own city rate of 1.93 per $100. Call the Trustee at (423) 209-7270 to confirm what your bill uses.

faqs.q: When are Hamilton County property taxes due?
faqs.a: From October 1 through the last day of February. Interest of 1.5 percent a month starts March 1. Notices go out near the end of September, though state law does not demand them.

faqs.q: How often does Hamilton County reappraise property?
faqs.a: Every four years. According to the Assessor's FAQ, the last reappraisal was in 2025 and the next comes in 2029. Between reappraisals, a record error can still be corrected on request.

faqs.q: Do I pay both Chattanooga and Hamilton County property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, a Chattanooga owner gets a county bill from the Trustee and a separate city bill from the City Treasurer. The Trustee also collects for seven other cities, among them East Ridge and Soddy Daisy.

faqs.q: Is there property tax relief for seniors in Hamilton County?
faqs.a: Yes. The state reimburses owners 65 or older whose income is under the limit, and the county matches the state amount. Chattanooga adds a freeze for seniors. Call (423) 209-7799 for an appointment.
